_comment: Single source of truth for GRIME's scoring model (Phase 5). scripts/check_model.py asserts the Python constants match this; keep them in sync.

hard_gates.note: apply_hard_gates (core/scoring.py) is the gate in use: velocity strictly < 3.0 m/s, width inclusive [0.5, 50.0], ownership strictly > 0. A second helper, passes_hard_gates (core/feasibility.py), is defined but called by no entry point and differs only at exactly 3.0 m/s. Fix-pass-2 Phase 3 adds the navigability gate: candidates within navigable_waterway_min_distance_m of a USACE National Waterway Network segment are excluded (a stationary net on legally navigable water — Section 10 — is unsafe/illegal); rows with no NWN data (NaN) pass, matching the gates-fire-only-on-real-values convention.

velocity_transport_favorability.applies: Flow sub-score only (M5): flow_velocity_ms is mapped through this peaked curve before MinMax normalization; the raw velocity still feeds velocity_feasibility and the hard gate.
velocity_transport_favorability.construct: Transport/delivery favorability (does the flow deliver debris to the site) — deliberately distinct from curves.velocity_feasibility (can a device operate there). The same raw velocity is scored through both curves because they measure different things.

bank_slope_input.source: NC OneMap / NC DPS DEM03 statewide lidar-derived elevation ImageServer
bank_slope_input.side_aggregation: mean of the steepest positive 5 m rise on each bank
bank_slope_input.fallback: Existing 10 m USGS 3DEP 3x3 DEM gradient when NC DEM03 samples are unavailable; non-NC regions retain this fallback.
bank_slope_input.provenance_note: USGS Seamless 1-m DEM coverage was verified incomplete in NC on 2026-07-12. DEM03 is the documented official-state-source fallback; it must not be labeled USGS 3DEP.

parameter_notes._comment: Status notes on parameters whose values are structurally constant or unpopulated in practice. The per-run varying/constant split is stamped into the output geojson's top-level 'provenance' block by scripts/score_candidates.py.
parameter_notes.bridge_proximity_bonus: Requires an NBI bridges layer that no shipped entry point supplies, so it evaluates to the 0.0 fallback (constant) and the constant-column drop renormalizes its weight away. Unpopulated — not a live driver of shipped scores.
parameter_notes.impervious_pct: NLCD imperviousness is fetched as a whole-bbox raster mean, so it is identical for every candidate within a run by construction (fallback 35.0 when the fetch fails).
parameter_notes.runoff_coeff_C: Derived from impervious_pct (C = 0.05 + 0.009*I), so it is constant whenever impervious_pct is.
parameter_notes.seasonal_cv: Inverted in scoring: steadier flow scores higher.
parameter_notes.normalization: Sub-scores MinMax-normalize each varying parameter within the candidate batch — including feasibility inputs that are already calibrated absolute [0,1] curve scores. Sub-scores are therefore batch-relative rankings, not absolute suitability values, and are not comparable across separately scored regions.

proximity_curves._comment: Impact-side proximity curves made LIVE by the fix-pass-2 Phase 1 wiring (EPA SEMS, USGS PAD-US 4.1, NC DEQ SWAP). The curve shapes/constants are the ones shipped in core/*.py all along (science freeze) — this block documents them and check_model.py guards them functionally.

superfund_score.source: EPA DataMap SEMS (sems.envirofacts_site), non-archived georeferenced sites, state-filtered

cso_density.source: EPA ECHO CSO inventory (national bulk), open CSO/TCS PF_LAT/PF_LON outfalls — same shared inverse-distance curve

litter_complaint_density.formula: sum over complaints of 1 / (1 + (distance_to_catchment_m / half_decay_m)^2) / catchment_area_km2
sources: Charlotte ServiceRequests311: LITTER/DEBRIS IN STREET + DUMPING IN STREET/ROW
Greensboro OpenData_CC_DS: 17-1 TW complaint-case archive joined to geocoded violations
litter_complaint_density.fallback: 0.0 where no public machine-readable litter/illegal-dumping feed exists or a configured feed is unavailable

protected_area_score.formula: sum over intersecting areas of weight(designation) * 1/(1 + d_km/decay_km)
protected_area_score.source: USGS PAD-US 4.1 state clip (local GDB preferred; official combined-inventory FeatureServer fallback), designation matched on d_Des_Tp/Des_Tp

water_intake_score.formula: sum over intakes within max_dist_km of exp(-d_km / decay_km)
water_intake_score.source: NC OneMap / NC DEQ SWAP public water supply sources, source_typ='Surface Water' (NC-only)

flood_regressions._comment: USGS SIR 2014-5030 Table 7 10%-AEP (Q10) regional regression equations, applied only inside each region's calibration domain (regions.json flood_method). DA in mi2, IMP = % impervious, I24H50Y = NOAA Atlas 14 24-h/50-y depth (in). Blue Ridge (HR2) has NO urban equation in the report ('methods are not applicable to urban streams in the Blue Ridge region') and stays flood_method none.

land_ownership._comment: Parcel owner-name -> land_ownership mapping (core/real_sources.py). Public 1.0, unknown 0.5; never 0.0 from ownership alone (0.0 would trip the hard gate). TOWN OF / VILLAGE OF are the fix-pass-2 statewide extension of the Durham-era hint list (same municipal-ownership construct).
